evals.prompt: ok so for my client's sweet shop we need a page for the diwali gift boxes. 3 box sizes, the client will give the prices later. the photos are in the drive folder diwali-2026, same look as their site, has to work on phone, whatsapp order button same number as the site. dont touch the home page. write me the prompt for codex
evals.expected_output: One copy-ready TCE block: a one-sentence Task; a Context of facts only that names the Drive folder and the existing site and marks the prices as [PENDING] instead of inventing them; Expectations that pin the output shape, list non-coder checks, carry the do-not lines (home page untouched, nothing new that was not asked), the [PENDING] instruction for the machine and the tell-before-change line. At most three questions, no preamble, no em-dashes, no sections or features the user did not ask for.
expectations: The answer contains three labelled sections in this order: Task, Context, Expectations
The Task section is exactly one sentence
The prices are marked as pending/unknown (e.g. [PENDING]) and no made-up price appears anywhere (a currency symbol inside a prohibition does not count)
The Context section contains no instructions to the AI (every line is a fact, a file, a link or a labelled assumption; no read/build/keep/do-not lines)
The Expectations section contains an explicit do-not line that the home page must not be changed
The Expectations section tells the AI to mark missing information as [PENDING] (or equivalent) instead of guessing
The Context section names the Drive folder diwali-2026 and the existing site as sources, and the WhatsApp number is taken from the site or marked pending, not invented
The Expectations section includes at least one check a non-coder could run (e.g. the page opens on a phone, the button opens WhatsApp)
The Expectations section includes the tell-before-change line: report which files or lines will change before changing anything
The prompt adds no page section, feature or deliverable the user did not ask for (no FAQ, no bulk or corporate block, no delivery block, no email signup)
The answer asks at most three questions
The answer contains no em-dash or en-dash characters
The prompt is delivered as one copyable block with no preamble explaining the method

evals.prompt: our menu page is live, people order from it every day. the paneer thali price shows 220 but it is 250 now. only that. last time i asked the AI to fix one price and it 'improved' the whole page and moved the photos around. what do i type this time?
evals.expected_output: A short TCE the owner can paste: Task is the single job (change the paneer thali price from 220 to 250 and nothing else); Context carries only facts (page live, orders daily, the price shows 220 today, the layout and photos are already correct); Expectations carry the do-not lines for layout, photos and every other price, 'nothing new I did not ask for', the tell-before-change line, and one check the owner can run. Fits on one screen, plain words, no jargon, no invented values.
expectations: The answer gives the owner one copyable prompt with labelled Task, Context, Expectations sections
The Task is a single job: change the paneer thali price from 220 to 250, nothing else
Expectations include explicit do-not lines covering the layout and the photos
Expectations include a do-not line that no other price or item changes
Expectations include 'do not add anything new that I did not ask for' or an equivalent scope lock
Expectations include the tell-before-change line: name which file and which line will change before changing anything, then wait
Context contains only facts (page is live, orders daily, price shows 220 today, layout and photos already correct) and no orders to the AI
Expectations include at least one check the owner can run without code (e.g. open the page on a phone, the thali shows 250, everything else looks the same as a before screenshot)
The answer invents no value the user did not give (no other prices, no colour codes, no file names, no page URL stated as fact; unknowns are marked pending or asked)
The whole answer fits on one screen: the prompt block is at most 22 lines and the total answer under 40 lines
No technical jargon a shop owner would not know (no CSS, dependency, refactor, DOM, selector, stylesheet, diff, git)
The answer contains no em-dash or en-dash characters

evals.prompt:
i asked codex for the whatsapp reminder text and this is what it gave me:

Hi Rohit! 🎉 Reminder: your free AI class is tomorrow at 10 AM at SCO 34, Sector 33D, Chandigarh. Limited seats, so come 15 minutes early and bring your laptop. See you there! 🙌

my spec was: a reminder sent 24 hours before the class. must have the student's name, the class time and the address. under 3 lines. no emoji. never say limited seats or anything like that. the facts i gave: Rohit, Saturday 10 AM, SCO 34 Sector 33D Chandigarh. did it make anything up? check it
evals.expected_output: The check, in order: (1) invented, not supported by spec or facts: 'come 15 minutes early', 'bring your laptop', 'free' and 'AI class' which were not in the facts, and the swap of the given fact 'Saturday' for 'tomorrow'; (2) every spec rule with a verdict: name met, time met or partly met, address met, under 3 lines with a verdict, no emoji NOT met (two emoji), no 'limited seats' NOT met, the 24-hour timing pending; (3) assumptions made without being told; (4) one line naming why; (5) a corrected text, written with [PENDING] markers where facts are missing, that itself passes the spec.
expectations: The answer flags 'come 15 minutes early' as not supported by the spec or the facts
The answer flags 'bring your laptop' as not supported by the spec or the facts
The answer flags the word 'free' as not among the facts the user gave
The answer flags the swap of the given fact 'Saturday' for 'tomorrow' (a fact replaced by a computed one)
The answer marks 'no emoji' as NOT met and identifies both emoji
The answer marks the 'never say limited seats' rule as NOT met
The answer marks name and address as met, matching the facts given
Every spec rule gets an explicit verdict (met / not met / pending), including the under-3-lines rule and the 24-hours-before rule
The answer lists assumptions the AI made without being told
The answer reports first and then offers a corrected reminder text as a separate step, not silently substituted for the report
The corrected reminder itself passes the spec: no emoji, no 'limited seats' or similar push, keeps 'Saturday', within 3 lines, and marks any fact it does not have as [PENDING] rather than guessing
The answer contains no em-dash or en-dash characters
